Quimby’s Bookstore Moving to a New Home on Union Avenue

by Emma DaveySeptember 2, 2026September 2, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:55
Instaread

The news that Crest Hardware was closing to make way for condos sent the neighborhood panicking about what else was on the chopping block. Crest neighbor Desert Island Comics decamped shortly after the news broke, due to a rent increase. Thankfully, they found a new home down the street. 

The indie bookstore Quimby’s (536 Metropolitan Ave.) operates out of the same address as Crest. Along with Desert Island, the block emerged as a hub for indie publishers where those whose tastes skewed a little more esoteric could find their niche.

Quimby’s owner Steven Svymbersky tells Greenpointers that he has now lost the lease, but thankfully, he found a new location just around the corner.

Svymbersky had been searching for a new Quimby’s home over the summer when a friend approached him with a possible deal—the space she owns at 418 Union Avenue.

“The space has the same square footage plus a backyard. The former tenant, Bibber & Bell Wine are closing September 1, 2026,” a press release reveals. “Quimby’s will begin building out the new store in October with an eye to being open by December 1, 2026.”

While Quimby’s first opened in Williamsburg in 2016, the store’s history dates much further back. Svymbersky opened the store in Chicago in 1991, a hub for books, zines, comics, and a plethora of off-the-beaten-path material. 

A friend created a crowdfunding campaign to help Quimby’s with the move, noting the importance of supporting the city’s remaining pockets of community spirit amid an era of instant deliveries from Amazon and big chains. 

“Uprooting and remodeling isn’t easy— the new space on Union needs to be retrofitted to accommodate new shelving, lighting, sound, signage, and general construction. It takes time and money to rebuild,” the Givebutter campaign reads.

Quimby’s rocks. It’s a one of a kind store in area that’s sadly been losing them. We’re thrilled they get to stay.
